items.content:
# Welcome to CS Studio

CS Studio is your all-in-one platform for learning computer science. Unlike traditional platforms that only offer multiple-choice questions or simple algorithmic puzzles, CS Studio provides a full-fledged cloud development environment.

## What can you do here?

- **Follow Curated Roadmaps:** From C Programming to AI/ML, we have structured paths.
- **Build Real Projects:** Use our web-based VS Code environment to build and compile actual software.
- **Track Progress:** Earn certificates and monitor your learning journey.

Let's dive in and start building!

items.content:
# Quickstart Guide

Getting your code running in CS Studio is incredibly simple.

## Step 1: Choose a Course or Roadmap
Navigate to the [Courses](/courses) or [Roadmaps](/roadmaps) section and select a topic you want to learn.

## Step 2: Open the IDE
Click on any coding challenge. This will launch the protected CS Studio IDE. 

## Step 3: Write & Compile
Write your code in the editor. When you are ready, click the **Compile & Run** button. The cloud compiler will execute your code and return the output instantly.

It's that easy!

items.content:
# Using the Cloud Compiler

The CS Studio cloud compiler allows you to run complex code without installing anything on your local machine.

## Supported Languages
Currently, the compiler supports:
- C/C++
- Java
- Python
- Node.js

## How it works securely
When you click 'Run', your code is sent to a secure, isolated Docker container in the cloud. It executes with restricted permissions to prevent malicious behavior, and the standard output is streamed directly back to your browser window via WebSockets.

items.content:
# Earning Certificates

Certificates prove that you have successfully completed a course and its associated capstone projects.

## Requirements
To earn a certificate for a specific course, you must:
1. Complete all theoretical modules.
2. Successfully pass all coding challenges.
3. Submit and pass the final capstone project.

## Verification
Every certificate comes with a unique cryptographic ID. Employers or peers can verify your certificate's authenticity by visiting the [Verify Certificate](/verify) page and entering your ID.
